extracted.intended_audience: federal agency program officers, grant administrators, pass-through entities, and prospective applicants for Federal financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing program planning, announcement, application, merit and risk review, specific award terms, and required contents and public reporting for Federal financial assistance under 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate type of Federal award
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency or pass-through entity must decide on the appropriate type of agreement for a Federal award (for example, a grant, cooperative agreement, subaward, or contract) in accordance with this guidance and the Federal Grant and Cooperative Agreement Act (31 U.S.C. 6301-6309).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select award instrument consistent with statutory authority and program design; see cross-reference to definitions in § 200.1 and other relevant sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for fixed amount awards
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal agency or pass-through entity may use fixed amount awards where the Federal award amount is negotiated using the cost principles as a guide; project scope has measurable goals and objectives; and accurate cost, historical, or unit pricing data exists to establish a fixed budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key conditions and rules include: accountability based on performance/results (not routine cost monitoring); permitted payment methods (partial payments with pre-agreed milestones, unit price basis, or single completion payment); prohibition in programs requiring cost sharing; program income may be generated but §200.307 does not apply; end-of-award written certification by recipient on completion and allowable expenditures with adjustments if activities were not completed; possible periodic reports; and prior approval requirements limited to specified paragraphs of §200.308(f) and §200.333. Record retention and audit availability still apply (§§200.334–200.338 and §200.101(b)(5)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program planning and design: goals and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: A program must be designed with clear goals and objectives that provide meaningful results and be consistent with the Federal authorizing legislation of the program, and to measure performance based on those goals and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance measures may differ by program type; see §200.301 for performance measurement. Design should align with agency strategic goals and reporting requirements (Part 6 of OMB Circular A‑11) and with applicable evidence and evaluation laws (PMIAA, Foundations for Evidence‑Based Policymaking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program planning and design: stakeholder engagement and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should encourage applicants to engage, when practicable, members of the community that will benefit from or be impacted by a program during design, and should develop programs in consultation with benefiting or impacted communities while considering available data, evidence, and past evaluation results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should make efforts to extend eligibility to all potential applicants and coordinate with other agencies where program goals align.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide public notice / Assistance Listings maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency must maintain an accurate list of Federal programs in the Assistance Listings maintained by GSA at SAM.gov and must assign the appropriate Assistance Listing before making the Federal award unless exigent circumstances require otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance Listings are the government-wide source; information submitted to GSA (in coordination with OMB) must follow prescribed format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required for Assistance Listing entries
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating an Assistance Listing, the Federal agency must submit: Program Description, Purpose, Goals, and Measurement; Identification (discretionary or non-discretionary); Projected total amount of funds available; Anticipated source of available funds; General eligibility requirements; and Applicability of Single Audit Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program descriptions should be plain language and aligned with agency performance plans and statutory requirements; projected funding estimates may use prior year funding if current appropriations unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of funding opportunities (NOFO) — open competition and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency must announce specific funding opportunities for Federal financial assistance that will be openly competed, communicate opportunities in plain language, limit length and complexity, and make technical assistance/clarifications accessible and widely available to all potential applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should be made to reach diverse and underserved applicants and to identify all eligible applicant types in the NOFO (e.g., nonprofit types, tribal organizations). Post clarifying Q&A (e.g., on Grants.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: NOFO summary information required on Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency must display on Grants.gov, preceding the full text, summary information including: Federal Agency Name; Funding Opportunity Title; Announcement Type; Funding Opportunity Number; Assistance Listing Number(s); Funding Details (expected total amount, anticipated number of awards, expected dollar values); Key Dates; Executive Summary (plain language, <=500 words); and Agency contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding details may be expressed as ranges or averages; if evaluating on a rolling basis, provide estimate of processing/notification time; key dates include release of application materials when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOFO availability period
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should make funding opportunities available for application for at least 60 calendar days, but may modify the period; however no funding opportunity should be available for less than 30 calendar days unless exigent circumstances justify a shorter period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be appropriate to provide technical assistance to unanticipated or inexperienced applicant pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full text of funding opportunities and application burden minimization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency must include the information in Appendix I for every funding opportunity, ensure funding opportunities are written using plain language, and streamline requirements to reduce application burden, considering whether requirements must be met at application or at award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly streamline NOFOs targeted to underserved or inexperienced applicants; programmatic/administrative requirements should be considered for timing (application vs award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review requirement and design
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless prohibited by statute, the Federal agency must design and execute a merit review process for discretionary Federal awards to select recipients most likely to be successful in delivering results based on program objectives; merit review must be objective and follow the agency's written standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards should identify number of reviewers required and provide opportunities for a diverse group of participants, including those representing underserved communities. The merit review process must be described or incorporated by reference in the NOFO (see Appendix I) and periodically reviewed by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of OMB-designated repositories prior to award
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making a Federal award, the agency is required to review eligibility and financial integrity information available in OMB-designated databases (Payment Integrity Information Act, Do Not Pay Initiative) and to review responsibility/qualification records in the non-public segment of SAM.gov when the Federal share is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must consider SAM.gov information for applicant and any immediate highest-level owner, predecessor, or subsidiary; satisfactory record of administering Federal awards, integrity, and business ethics should be demonstrated. Agencies may still make awards with mitigation (specific conditions) where appropriate (§200.208).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment policy and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies must establish and maintain policies and procedures for conducting a risk assessment to evaluate risks posed by applicants before issuing Federal awards, to identify risks affecting achievement of project goals and to determine appropriate oversight and monitoring resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk assessments may incorporate elements such as application quality, award amount, program risk, cybersecurity, fraud risks, and local impacts. If award is made, specific conditions may address assessed risks. Risk criteria must be described in the funding announcement (§200.204).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk criteria items to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating applicant risk, agencies should consider: (i) financial stability; (ii) management systems and standards; (iii) history of performance on Federal awards (including reporting compliance); (iv) audit reports and findings; and (v) ability to effectively implement statutory/regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items help determine need for specific conditions, level of monitoring, or other mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to risk assessment during performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency may modify the risk assessment at any time during the period of performance, which may justify changes to the terms and conditions of the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should implement adjustments and corresponding specific conditions as risk profiles change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and debarment compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and recipients must comply with nonprocurement debarment and suspension regulations implementing Executive Orders 12549 and 12689 and with 2 CFR part 180, which restrict awards to parties that are debarred, suspended, or otherwise excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must require recipient compliance and use available exclusions when assessing eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard application requirements and Paperwork Reduction Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies may only use application information collections approved by OMB under the Paperwork Reduction Act and should align with OMB-approved government-wide data elements; examples include Standard Form 424 and the Biographical Sketch Common Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB will authorize additional collections only on a limited basis. Agencies may inform applicants when they need not submit information already collected through other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose specific conditions in awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies are responsible for ensuring that specific Federal award conditions and performance expectations are consistent with program design and may adjust specific conditions based on review of OMB-designated data, recipient compliance history, expected ability to meet performance goals, or inadequate financial capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific conditions may include: requiring reimbursement payments rather than advances; withholding authority to proceed to next phase until evidence of acceptable performance; requiring additional or more detailed financial reports; additional project monitoring; requiring technical or management assistance; and establishing additional prior approvals. Agencies must notify recipients of the nature, reason, corrective actions, time allowed, and reconsideration method prior to imposing conditions, and must promptly remove conditions once issues are resolved (§200.208).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and representations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal agency or pass-through entity is authorized to require a recipient to submit annual certifications and representations, and submission may be required more frequently if a recipient fails to meet a requirement of a Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a recipient is provided an exception to requirements of 2 CFR 25.110, the recipient must submit the appropriate assurance form (e.g., SF‑424B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award costs rule reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements on costs incurred by the applicant prior to the start date of the period of performance are governed by §200.458.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and applicants must consult §200.458 for allowable pre-award cost conditions and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required to be included in a Federal award
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Federal award must include performance goals (where applicable) and specified general Federal award information such as: Recipient Name (matching unique entity identifier), Recipient's Unique Entity Identifier, Unique Federal Award Identification Number (FAIN), Federal Award Date, Period of Performance start/end, Budget Period start/end, Amount of Federal Funds Obligated by this Action, Total Amount of Federal Funds Obligated, Total Approved Cost Sharing (if applicable), Total Amount of Federal Award including approved Cost Sharing, Budget Approved by the Federal Agency, Federal Award Description (statutory compliance), Name of the Federal agency and awarding official contact, Assistance Listings Number and Title, Identification whether the Award is R&D, and Indirect Cost Rate (including de minimis if charged per §200.414).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, include performance goals, indicators, targets, baseline data, and specify how/when performance will be assessed (§§200.202 and 200.301).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of general terms and conditions in awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies must incorporate certain general terms and conditions either in the Federal award or by reference, including administrative requirements, national policy requirements, recipient integrity and performance matters (when total Federal share may exceed $500,000), future budget period conditions, and termination provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain the general terms and conditions on their website, provide the full text upon request, and archive previous versions with effective dates for recipients, auditors, or others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal award specific terms and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must include any specific terms and conditions in each Federal award that are in addition to general terms and conditions, and for loan/loan guarantee programs must specify continuing compliance requirements where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever practicable, specific terms and conditions should be available on the agency's website and in NOFOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to Federal award information
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must publish required Federal award information on USAspending.gov per OMB and Treasury Government-wide Spending Data Model guidance; responsibility and qualification records posted in SAM.gov are publicly available after a 14-calendar day waiting period subject to limited exceptions and FOIA exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to public posting include certain past performance reviews, pre-April 15, 2011 entries, and withdrawn information during the waiting period. Agencies must respect FOIA and controlled unclassified information exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting determinations that an applicant is not qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency determines it will not make an award because the applicant does not meet minimum qualification standards based solely on prior record of performance or integrity and the award was expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold, the agency must report that determination in SAM.gov and notify the applicant with a brief explanation and information on rights and system retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported information remains in system for five years; agencies must allow applicants to review and comment and must consider comments in future qualification determinations. Agencies must correct erroneous entries within three business days and amend helpful updates within 30 days. Agencies must not post FOIA-exempt information in the public segment and must remove postings within seven calendar days if a recipient asserts FOIA exemption applicability while resolving via FOIA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain telecommunications and video surveillance equipment or services
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and subrecipients are prohibited from obligating or expending funds to procure or renew covered telecommunications equipment or services as defined in section 889 of Public Law 115‑232, including specific manufacturers (Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, Dahua) and equipment/services owned or controlled by covered foreign countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered equipment also includes systems using such equipment as a substantial or essential component. Agency heads must prioritize funding and technical support to assist affected entities to transition from covered equipment. Acceptance of a grant certifies recipient will comply with this prohibition; see §200.471 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never Contract with the Enemy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies, recipients, and subrecipients are subject to guidance implementing Never Contract with the Enemy (2 CFR part 183), which affects covered contracts, grants, and cooperative agreements expected to exceed $50,000, performed outside the United States and its territories, and in support of contingency operations with active hostilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and recipients must follow part 183 provisions when contracts/grants meet thresholds and context described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower protections for recipient employees
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee of a recipient or subrecipient must not be discharged, demoted, or otherwise discriminated against as reprisal for disclosing information the employee reasonably believes is evidence of gross mismanagement, gross waste of Federal funds, abuse of authority, substantial and specific danger to public health or safety, or violation of law related to a Federal contract or grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients and subrecipients must inform employees in writing of whistleblower rights and protections under 41 U.S.C. 4712 and related statutory provisions (10 U.S.C. 4701, 41 U.S.C. 4712, 41 U.S.C. 4304, 10 U.S.C. 4310).
